candidate_comparison.summary: Single closed cut-gem body with real table/crown/girdle/pavilion planar facets.
candidate_comparison.strength: Facet grammar is intrinsic to the object, so silhouette, highlight and refraction all agree.
candidate_comparison.risk: Requires disciplined topology and facet count.

candidate_comparison.summary: Single thick clear crystal solid with a broad flat optical window and geometry-native faceted perimeter.
candidate_comparison.strength: Preserves premium clarity in the center while concentrating sparkle and cut grammar at the edge.
candidate_comparison.risk: Can read as plain glass if the edge cut or thickness is too weak.

candidate_comparison.summary: Geometry Nodes driven irregular facet/cell system.
candidate_comparison.risk: Can drift toward cracked-ice/noise and repeat the procedural-look failure.

visual_grammar: A-family true front faceting rejected below 90 because full-face facet patterns read opaque/fractured
B1 clean windowed solid improved premium clarity but read too close to plain glass
B2 keeps a broad flat front optical window and moves complex facet grammar to a real rear pavilion
rear pavilion is geometry-native and ordered, intended to create a controlled internal starburst through refraction
32-sided front/girdle preserves a near-round premium silhouette
central MorphMint bar remains a shallow frosted crystal inset
